raw_response:
For the one-to-three-person lodging-reservation example, I would start by evaluating **Laravel with Filament**. **Django with Celery** is the closest alternative, especially if the team already works in Python. Rails remains a plausible third option, but I have not verified a complete admin/authentication configuration in this search.

The supplied summary asks for a framework supporting CRUD, authentication, admin, background jobs, mail, and files. It does not specify a language, database, hosting platform, price constraint, or a requirement that all six features live in the framework core. I have therefore compared framework-based stacks and made the added components explicit. The ranking is a judgment about the documented fit, not a measured claim about development speed.

### 1. Laravel with Filament — strongest documented fit

Laravel's official documentation describes authentication guards and providers, authentication starter kits, background queues, mailables, and a filesystem abstraction. Filament supplies the admin interface, with documentation for listing, creating, editing, viewing, and deleting records. This maps directly onto the requested capability set. Sources: [authentication](https://laravel.com/framework/docs/9.x/authentication), [queues](https://laravel.com/framework/docs/9.x/queues), [mail](https://laravel.com/framework/docs/9.x/mail), [files](https://laravel.com/framework/docs/9.x/filesystem), and [Filament admin installation](https://filamentphp.com/docs/2.x/admin/installation).

For the inspected historical configuration, Filament 2.x documents Laravel v8.0+, PHP 8.0+, and Livewire v2.0+ requirements. The installation instructions explicitly require additional access configuration for production administration. Laravel's queue documentation offers several backends, including a database connection; the mail API can enqueue delivery; and the filesystem documentation covers local and remote storage. These are capabilities to configure, not an already implemented reservation product.

I would use the framework for the main application and Filament for staff management of the application's records. The team must still build the customer-facing reservation flow and its domain rules. **Assessment: DIRECT_DOCUMENTED for the broad requested capabilities in the proposed stack.** Some supporting authentication, queue, and mail details came from substantive official search excerpts; the direct-open displays for those pages were limited to navigation. No application was installed or tested.

### 2. Django with Celery — strong alternative, one verification gap

Django's official documentation covers its model/query layer, automatic internal admin, email APIs, and uploaded-file/storage APIs. Celery's official guide documents integration with a Django project, including shared settings and task discovery. Sources: [Django documentation](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.1/), [admin](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.1/ref/contrib/admin/), [email](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.1/topics/email/), [files](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.1/topics/files/), and [Celery integration](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/v5.2.7/django/first-steps-with-django.html).

The admin documentation makes an important boundary clear: its intended role is internal management. Public booking screens still need their own views. Celery is an additional task-processing component to configure and operate; this proposal does not claim Django 4.1 itself includes the queue runner.

An official [Django authentication result](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.1/topics/auth/) appeared in search, but I did not open that page. **Assessment: INSUFFICIENT for a completely verified setup in this run, not a known failure.** Confirm the intended authentication setup against the chosen version's documentation. Positive evidence would close the remaining broad capability gap; an explicit unsupported requirement would change the assessment for that configuration. If the team already knows Django well, that existing knowledge could reasonably move it ahead of Laravel.

### 3. Ruby on Rails — plausible, but less completely verified here

The [Rails 7.0.4 introductory guide](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/v7.0.4/getting_started.html) explicitly lays out CRUD operations and identifies Action Mailer, Active Job, and Active Storage. That makes Rails worth evaluating for the same application scope.

I attempted the [ActiveAdmin installation page](https://activeadmin.info/0-installation.html), but it returned only a relocation notice. I have not established the compatible admin/authentication package versions or the selected background-job backend. **Assessment: INSUFFICIENT.** Keep Rails on the shortlist while verifying that concrete combination; the evidence gap does not establish that Rails cannot meet the requirements.

### How I would make the choice

With no existing language preference stated, Laravel plus Filament is my first candidate from the evidence gathered. I would compare it with Django plus Celery using one representative application slice: a staff-managed lodging record, an authenticated customer action, a stored file, and an asynchronously sent email. That is a proposed evaluation step, not an evaluation performed here.

The question is dated September 27, 2022. I used older versioned documentation where practical, but those pages were retrieved live in 2026 and their exact historical revisions are unknown. Newer Django task-framework and Rails authentication-generator search results were not used to backdate capabilities. The old versions cited here identify the evidence scope; they are not a recommendation to deploy unsupported versions today. Anonymous GitHub code search was attempted and blocked, and the code-through-web fallback did not produce usable code evidence.

checks.name: Jekyll without an additional backend
checks.reason: Jekyll's official quickstart and setup guide define a build-time static-site generator whose output is a directory of static files. The supplied no-additional-backend configuration leaves that static output as the whole proposal, which does not perform the runtime booking-application role covering the requested CRUD, authentication, admin, jobs, mail, and files. This is a documented operating-scope mismatch; adding an application backend would change the supplied candidate.
checks.verification_status: Official static-output architecture and development-server behavior read. Individual unsupported-feature statements were not invented from documentation silence.
